gen_risks.description: Short construction season may cause delays if the transmission line is not completed before winter.
gen_risks.mitigation: Plan civil works to start early in the season, incorporate buffer time in the schedule, and use fast‑track construction techniques.
gen_risks.evidence: If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays with waiting for the next construction season.

gen_risks.description: Absence of domestic manufacturers for 220 kV poles and conductors may lead to supply delays and quality issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pre‑qualify qualified foreign suppliers, secure early contracts, and implement strict quality‑control inspections on all imported components.
gen_risks.evidence: no local company who can produce metal poles and conductors meeting the standards for 220kV lines

gen_risks.description: Extreme wind, snow, earthquake and flood hazards could damage towers and reduce line reliability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate‑resilient engineering standards, conduct site‑specific hazard modelling, and use higher‑grade materials and foundations.
gen_risks.evidence: enhanced engineering and design standards that consider wind loading, snow, freezing, earthquake and flood

gen_risks.description: Transmission line may increase bird collisions and impact avifauna biodiversity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Install bird‑friendly flight diverters, realign the route away from key habitats, and monitor avian mortality during operation.
gen_risks.evidence: Transmission lines in Mongolia often involve bird collision... Bird management Plan adjusted route

gen_risks.description: Construction and operation expose workers to OHS risks such as falls, electrocution and EMF exposure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and enforce a comprehensive OHS plan, provide safety training, use insulated tools, and conduct regular site inspections.
gen_risks.evidence: OHS risks associated with live power lines, working at height, electric and magnetic fields (EMF)

gen_risks.description: New PMO lacks experienced financial management staff, risking ineffective fund administration.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified financial officers early, provide bank‑led training, and establish mentorship with experienced staff from previous energy projects.
gen_risks.evidence: PMO not yet in place and no financial management staff has been appointed

gen_risks.description: Weak internal financial controls may lead to unauthorized expenditures or misreporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize and implement a detailed Financial Management Manual with segregation of duties, approval matrices and regular internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Weak internal controls: There are not any internal controls related financial management policies and procedures established

gen_risks.description: A significant share of locally sourced construction materials may be sub‑standard, causing rework and cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Introduce mandatory material testing, enforce compliance with international specifications, and retain a contingency budget for material replacement.
gen_risks.evidence: 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market

gen_risks.description: Inadequate budgeting could result in funds being spent on non‑project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare annual budgets aligned to procurement plans, conduct quarterly variance analysis, and require PSC approval for any re‑allocations.
gen_risks.evidence: Poor budgeting: The project funds not used for the intended purposes

gen_risks.description: Evaluation Committee’s limited English proficiency may delay assessment of international bids.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide English‑language training for committee members and use bilingual procurement consultants to translate and review documents promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation Committee members normally do not have knowledge and experience in handling English documents, may cause delays

gen_risks.description: Frequent changes of decision‑making officials can interrupt procurement and contract approvals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize delegation of authority in the Project Operational Manual and maintain a continuity log for all key contacts.
gen_risks.evidence: Frequent change of the decision-making officials for the Project

gen_risks.description: Seasonal nature of civil works restricts construction to a narrow window, increasing likelihood of schedule slippage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Advance procure long‑lead items, mobilize contractors before the season starts, and negotiate penalty/bonus clauses for timely completion.
gen_risks.evidence: seasonal nature of civil works in Mongolia adds more risks... one construction season

gen_risks.description: Ineffective grievance redress could lead to community opposition and project stoppages.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a two‑stage GRM with clear timelines, conduct regular community outreach, and track resolution metrics publicly.
gen_risks.evidence: Project level grievance redress mechanism (GRM) will replicate the mechanisms used under previous World Bank-financed projects

gen_risks.description: Construction activities may temporarily restrict herders’ access to pasture and water sources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Coordinate with local soum authorities to schedule works around grazing periods and provide alternative water points where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders (for example, pasture, wells, etc.)

gen_risks.description: Potential change of government officials after elections could affect project continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage re‑elected officials early, secure written commitments, and maintain a stakeholder coalition supporting the project.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential changes in Government officials involved in project activities due to election cycle

gen_risks.description: Current electricity tariffs are below cost, risking utility cash‑flow and ability to pay for the new line.
gen_risks.mitigation: Coordinate with the Energy Regulatory Commission to advance tariff reform and incorporate cost‑recovery mechanisms in the loan agreement.
gen_risks.evidence: Current electricity price is below the cost of service causing financial difficulties for sector utilities

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related hazards (floods, wildfires, landslides) could damage the transmission corridor.
gen_risks.mitigation: Select route through low‑risk terrain, incorporate erosion control measures, and design towers for extreme weather survivability.
gen_risks.evidence: Mongolia is prone to risks from climate hazards such as flooding, wildfires, and landslides

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private investment in VRE may limit the anticipated renewable capacity enabled by the line.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer grid‑access incentives, publish a transparent curtailment‑reduction framework, and conduct investor outreach workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: estimated only 100 MW will be developed by private investors

gen_risks.description: Limited procurement capacity of local firms may lead to contract performance issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted procurement training, use an Owner’s Engineer to monitor contractor performance, and enforce qualified‑bidder criteria.
gen_risks.evidence: many of them lack human resources... no local company ... can produce metal poles

gen_risks.description: Heavy reliance on imported construction materials exposes the project to border closures or pandemic‑related supply disruptions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a diversified supplier base, maintain strategic stock of critical items, and include force‑majeure clauses in supply contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: 75-80% of construction materials are sourced from outside the country

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risks are rated Substantial. The parliamentary election was held in June 2024 and a new coalition government was formed, with representation of all three major political parties. While there may be risks of disagreement on the approval of individual projects, these risks will be mitigated by the strong alignment of the proposed operation with the NRP and the new Government Action Plan for 2024-2028.
gt_risks.mitigation: Continued engagement with key stakeholders, including government and the parliament, through ongoing analytical and technical support on VRE integration and energy sector reform, will help mitigate risks going forward. The Development Partner Group, co-chaired by the World Bank and UNDP, will also offer a donor coordination platform to maintain political momentum for RE integration.

gt_risks.description: The macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. Mongolia's economic outlook is dependent on global macroeconomic factors, in particular commodity prices. Despite recent positive short-term developments from coal and agricultural exports, Mongolia still needs to strengthen fiscal and external buffers to respond to future shocks and continue reforms aimed at diversifying the economy.
gt_risks.mitigation: To mitigate these risks and manage external balances, the World Bank has been, and will continue to be, supporting the authorities in restoring fiscal and external buffers through analytical and advisory work.

gt_risks.description: The sector strategies and policies risk is rated Substantial. Substantial risk still exists due to institutional fragmentation, lack of policies to promote RE projects, and lack of clear commitment of reforms, especially related to tariff reforms that are crucial to make the sector viable and be able to refinance projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include actively engaging in multi-stakeholder coordination meetings and providing technical advice and capacity building to key stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: The institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk is rated Substantial. The implementing agency MOE and NPTG have experience implementing World Bank-funded projects; however, there is a substantial risk that newly hired PMO staff may not have sufficient capacity, which could potentially lead to implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The PMO will be strengthened with experienced consultants and targeted training and capacity building. Mitigating measures include the World Bank's scrutiny of PMO members' selection, including a review of the TOR and providing no objection to the qualification criteria of the staff.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. There are substantial risks due to the reliance of MOE on a newly constituted PMO, which may cause delays in processing payments, conducting IFRs, and other reporting requirements; the construction sector in Mongolia is often subject to delays and cost overruns. Potential procurement risks include (i) likelihood of time and cost overruns due to weak contract management capacity, and (ii) significant procurement delays due to delayed initiation of procurement and establishment of needed staffing arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: Capacity building through customized training and TA is a central element of the Project, along with strong project supervision and contract management capacity building; MOE will continue to directly provide intensive support to the PMO. Procurement risks are mitigated by (a) establishing a PMO with appropriate procurement and technical staff per FIDIC contract standards; (b) clearly defined workflow in decision-making within the MOE/PMO procurement manual; and (c) extensive market engagement to stimulate market participation.
